## Positioning

Mission: Build AI capability from within. Build. Advise. Invest.

Freedom with AI advises founders, CEOs and leadership teams in space, defense and complex technology businesses on AI strategy, adoption and company growth. Its work combines executive experience, practical AI product building and an ongoing outside perspective, helping leaders set direction and their teams put it into practice. The firm also invests its own capital in space and physical AI companies.

The firm's depth is in software, product, AI and executive leadership, not aerospace engineering.

## Thesis

AI is leaving the screen, and space is its hardest test.

The money has moved in three steps, following Cammie Clay's State of AI: Investing talk:

- Bits (2010s to 2024): software eats the world through SaaS, apps and per-seat pricing. Investors rewarded growth and seats.
- Bits buy atoms (2025 to 2026): AI money pours into chips, data centers and power. Investors reward revenue and retention, not demos.
- Bits drive atoms (2027 and beyond): AI goes into the real world through robotaxis already on the road, then robots, devices and AI-designed drugs. Investors will reward a physical moat: hardware, real-world data and regulation.

The firm's focus is the next step: space. Software alone gets copied in months. Software plus the real world is hard to copy, and space is the hardest real world there is.

### The stack in space

The five-layer stack builds on Jensen Huang's framing of AI as infrastructure. The space mapping is the firm's own.

- Applications and embodied AI. On Earth: robots, vehicles, scientific tools and other systems that sense, decide and act. In space: imagery, connectivity, logistics and servicing in orbit.
- Models. On Earth: frontier, open-source and domain-specific models. In space: onboard autonomy, because spacecraft cannot wait for a round trip to Earth to make every decision.
- Infrastructure. On Earth: data centers, networking, cooling, orchestration and security. In space: downlinks, ground networks and compute in orbit.
- Chips and compute. On Earth: processors, memory, interconnects and supply. In space: compute that survives radiation, heat and a tight power budget.
- Energy. On Earth: the constraint under everything. In orbit: literally finite, with every subsystem competing for it.

### Why space

- The moat is physical. Hardware in orbit, real-world data and hard-won licenses are hard to copy.
- Every AI constraint is sharper. Power, compute, bandwidth and latency are tighter in space.
- Leadership is the bottleneck. Many space companies have the engineering; fewer have the leadership, product direction and internal capability to turn it into a durable business.

### Where the firm contributes

Technology creates possibilities. Leadership determines how a company puts them to work.

The firm advises founders, CEOs and leadership teams on AI, product and technology strategy, connecting technical capabilities with customer needs, business priorities and organizational capability. Its work spans building new products and businesses, adopting AI across functions, developing leaders and identifying opportunities in proprietary data. It brings an ongoing outside perspective while helping companies strengthen the capabilities of their own people.

### How the firm participates

- Advise, led by Sonia Sarao: executive advisory for founders, CEOs and leadership teams in space, defense and complex technology businesses, on AI strategy, adoption and company growth.
- Invest, led by Cammie Clay: the firm's own capital in early-stage space companies, and physical AI where it meets space.
- Build: the firm builds AI products as well as advising on them. faibuddy.com, an AI-native advisory product for entrepreneurs, is live.

## Advisory

Executive advisory for AI strategy: build AI capability from within. Clients work directly with Sonia Sarao to connect AI opportunities with business priorities, executive leadership and the capabilities of their internal teams. For founders, CEOs and leadership teams in space, defense and complex technology businesses.

### Focus areas

- AI strategy and executive leadership: identify where AI can create business value, establish priorities and help leaders shape the organization and culture to support them.
- AI adoption across functions: help teams evaluate tools, improve workflows and build skills and systems that can evolve as AI advances.
- Product and data strategy: identify opportunities for AI in products and services, and how proprietary data can strengthen customer value and competitive advantage.

### Experience across the business

Sonia's advisory work draws on experience with product direction, customer discovery, new business lines, enterprise growth, global teams, fundraising and acquisition diligence. She also coaches founders and CEOs on executive leadership, organizational development and culture.

### When leaders bring the firm in

- AI is on the leadership agenda, and the priorities are not yet set
- Teams are trying AI tools, but the way work gets done has not changed
- Proprietary data could strengthen the product, and no one owns that decision
- A new product or business line needs direction and an owner
- The company is growing faster than its leadership structure
- An acquisition, partnership or raise is on the horizon, and the plan has to hold up to scrutiny

### How the firm works

Ongoing executive advisory and fractional leadership engagements, shaped around the company's priorities. Regular working sessions and direct access provide continuity as decisions move into practice. Sonia brings an ongoing outside perspective on AI while working alongside the company's leadership and internal teams. The scope, cadence and fee reflect the priorities and level of involvement. Start at https://freedomwith.ai/advisory#start.

### Selected advisory work

- B2B software: a growth-stage company needed its enterprise segments, product strategy and AI direction to reinforce the same business model.
- FinTech: the company was shaping its product, target market and business model around the regulatory requirements that defined what the product could become.
- Life sciences: the company needed to align its target market, product and operating model with the compliance requirements affecting them.

These examples are anonymized and describe work actually performed.

## Investing

The firm writes early, small checks with its own money in space companies, and in physical AI where it meets space. Where a company needs deep aerospace or hardware diligence, it invests alongside specialist investors.

What it looks for:

- Technology that works, or is close, with a clear path to a paying customer
- Founders who want a partner in AI strategy, product and company growth, as well as capital
- Markets where software, data and AI compound a hardware advantage
- A round where the firm can be useful beyond the capital

Founders the firm backs can draw on Cammie's experience in diligence, risk and governance, and Sonia's experience in AI strategy, product, executive leadership and company growth. Advisory and investing are separate decisions. Working with the firm does not require or promise an investment. Investing enquiries and introductions: https://freedomwith.ai/contact?topic=investing

## Partners

### Sonia Sarao, Co-Founder & Executive Advisor

Sonia advises founders, CEOs and leadership teams on AI, product and technology strategy, executive leadership and growth. She has spent more than 20 years in enterprise software and financial-market infrastructure, including a decade at NYSE. She was the first product hire at Fluxx and rose to VP of Product and Engineering as recurring revenue grew roughly tenfold, then became VP of Product at Groove. She helped win multimillion-dollar enterprise deals alongside Sales, developed new products and business lines, and supported Series A and B fundraising. She worked through diligence on three potential transactions at Fluxx, and led product at Groove through its completed acquisition by Clari. She has built and led technical teams across the US, India, Kenya, Canada and Europe, and holds degrees in computer science and software engineering. She built and launched faibuddy.com, an AI-native advisory product for entrepreneurs. Her depth is in software, product, AI and executive leadership, not aerospace engineering.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/sonia-sarao/

### Cammie Clay, Co-Founder, Investing

Cammie leads investing at Freedom with AI. She is a seasoned trader and public markets investor. She worked on both sides of financial regulation: enforcement and investigations at the New York Stock Exchange and FINRA, then compliance leadership at RS Investments and First Republic Bank, where she was VP of Compliance in private wealth management. She holds a Series 7. Her regulatory background is in financial markets; in space she brings a diligence, risk and governance lens rather than sector-specific licensing expertise.

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/cammieclay/
